AGENDA ITEMS AND ACTIONS
PUBLIC INFORMATION

The public may address the members of the City Council on any matters within the jurisdiction of the City Council or on any items on the agenda of the City Council during the designated public comment periods. There will be two Oral Communication sessions: one for Agendized Items (comment about items ON the agenda) and the other for non-Agendized items (comment about items NOT on the Agenda). The Oral Communications portion of the agenda is limited to a duration of one hour unless otherwise approved by the City Council. Comment time is normally 3 minutes depending on the number of speakers.

PUBLIC VIEWING AVAILABLE BY:

- Livestream on the City’s website: The meeting will be streamed live over the internet via: www.carsonca.gov or on Youtube: www.youtube.com/c/CityofCarsonCaliforniaOfficialYouTubePage
 
- Cable TV: Spectrum (Channel 35) and ATT (Channel 99)

IF YOU ARE NOT ABLE TO ATTEND THE MEETING IN-PERSON, PUBLIC COMMENTS CAN BE SUBMITTED BEFORE THE MEETING AT/VIA:

- Email: Public comments can be emailed to cityclerk@carsonca.gov. The cut-off time to submit any email communications is 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting.
 
- Written: Written comments can be dropped off at the City Clerk’s Office or in the white box outside City Hall. The cut-off time to submit any written communications is 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Written comments dropped off at the City Clerk’s Office or at the white box or any email received will not be read aloud at Council Meeting but will be circulated to the City Council and incorporated into the record.

3.. REPORT FROM CAPTAIN JONES OF CARSON SHERIFF'S STATION City Manager Roberts introduced Nora Garcia, Emergency Services Manager and acting Public Safety Manager
Surveillance camera and access control multimillion dollar project with Johnson Controls.

In October there was an uptick in crime so as a result Nora worked with Johnson Control to speed up the timeline for installation from 12 months to six months. 

November 7th, council approved the temporary cameras to be deployed in the parks. 
The intercoms at the loading docks and ECE have been replaced. 

License Plate Recognition Project- 80 cameras in the system. 
Contract awarded March 2023. Stolen vehicle stats have already improved in one month.
Mayor Davis-Holmes thanked Nora and asked if the mini parks can be added to the project. Nora shared that they can be added in phase 2. 
Councilman Hicks asked about the pools. Nora shared that they are.
He also asked about signage and wants notifications at entry points or through a press release so everyone knows they are being watched. City Manager Roberts replied that it will be announced via social media, radio edits, and streaming devices.
MPT Hilton thanked Public Safety department and that this project is a wonderful thing to protect our residents. 
Councilwoman Rojas thanked the department and shared how important it is to stay up to date and the cameras are important for safety.
Councilman Dear shared that the cameras represent a key part in safety for the residents. Public Safety is very important to him. He mentioned the 27% increase in stolen car recovery.

In response to MPT's concerns about crime related to the hotel changes. Communication was made with the manager of Home Keep 3.0 partnership between the state and county. They will renovate and create 107 studio style apartments for families who are currently facing homelessness. Time frame for this project is uncertain at this time. 
Safety tips to prevent becoming a victim of people pretending to work for a security company: 
Do not feel like you have to let them in your home. Do not open the door. Be cautious of uniforms and identification. Even if you do schedule, do not allow anyone in your home unsupervised. If something feels out of place, do not hesitate to reach out to the Carson Sheriffs Station. 
2023 Crime Stats- 2,620 arrests, 119 were firearm related (158 firearms taken off the street) 37,589 calls for service, 27,418 self initiated crime prevention scenarios, 12,735 reports written, responded to calls between 4-37 minutes, major crimes were reduced. Overall crime reduced by 2% as a result of community policing, town halls, use of social media, continued collaboration of city leadership, etc. 
Mayor Davis-Holmes shared that she would like Captain Jones to sit in on upcoming meetings with the owner and management of the hotel project. The place has been sold since December 20th so the current inhabitants are just making as much money as they can so the mayor has asked for additional coverage.
